SPICE solver

A small SPICE-style circuit simulator: modified nodal analysis, Newton iteration for nonlinear devices.

pip install -r requirements.txt python main.py # opens the window; pick a netlist with the file dialog python main.py examples/rc.cir # opens the window with a netlist already loaded python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

Needs Python 3.12+ with tkinter (included with Python; on Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install python3-tk), plus numpy, scipy, matplotlib and customtkinter (see requirements.txt).

Using the window

  • Open netlist… (or Ctrl+O) shows your system's file explorer. The chosen file is simulated straight away; Run again (or F5) re-reads it from disk, so you can edit in any editor and re-run.
  • Results shows each analysis as a table (long transients show 2000 evenly spaced rows). If the netlist has several analyses, a selector above the tabs switches between them.
  • Plot draws the selected analysis: lines for .dc/.ac/.tran, bars for .op. Probes of different kinds (v, vdb, vp, i ...) get separate axes, so a Bode plot has magnitude over phase. The toolbar zooms, pans and saves the image.
  • Netlist shows the file with line numbers, so "line 7" in an error can be found at once. Messages lists warnings and errors.
  • Export CSV… asks where to save the selected analysis, with every point.
  • Transient method and Appearance (system / light / dark) are in the sidebar.

The command line is also available: python cli.py circuit.cir [--csv DIR] [--method backward_euler].

Supported netlist features

Devices R C L V I D Q M, and X subcircuit instances (nesting allowed)
Sources [dc] v, dc v, ac mag [phase], SIN PULSE PWL EXP
Models .model of type d npn pnp nmos pmos (D: is n bv ibv; BJT: is bf br vaf; MOS level 1: vto kp lambda, instance w l m)
Analyses .op, .dc (one source), .ac dec/oct/lin, .tran [tstart [tmax]] [uic]
Output .print/.plot/.probe: v(n) v(a,b) i(dev) vdb vp vm vr vi (and i*), ic ib ie (BJT), id ig is (MOSFET). With none given, all node voltages and voltage-source currents are shown
Other .subckt/.ends, .options (gmin reltol vntol abstol itl1), .title, .end

Anything that would silently change the answer is an error (.param, .include, area factors, unknown device letters ...). Things that cannot be honoured but only mildly affect results (.ic, .nodeset, .temp, model parameters that are not modelled, the MOSFET bulk node) produce a warning on stderr.

Layout

main.py              graphical front end (starts gui.py)
gui.py               the window: file dialog, worker thread, tabs
plotting.py          matplotlib figures for a Solution (no GUI toolkit needed)
cli.py               command-line front end
spiceParser.py       netlist text -> Netlist; subcircuit flattening
simulate.py          runs each analysis, returns uniform `Solution`s
probes.py, report.py probe expressions; text/CSV output
circuit/             devices (parse + stamp), terminals, sources, model cards, graph builder
solver/              MNA system, Newton, DC/AC/transient analyses, waveforms
graph.py             generic hypergraph the circuit is stored in
util/                number syntax, validation helpers
tests/, examples/

Notes

  • Currents follow the solver's convention: a device's current flows from its first terminal through it to its second, so a voltage source that is delivering power reports a negative current (as in SPICE).
  • A PMOS vto is negative for an enhancement device, as in SPICE (it is normalised internally).
  • In .tran, tstep is also the integration step (reduced to tmax if smaller), the circuit is solved on a fixed grid, and tstart only hides the early part of the output. Trapezoidal integration treats a source that jumps between grid points as a ramp across the step; use --method backward_euler or a smaller step for sharp edges.

circuit/circuit.py

 1from collections.abc import Hashable, Iterable
 2
 3from circuit.components import Component
 4from circuit.terminals import Terminals
 5from errors import CircuitError, SpiceError
 6from graph import Hypergraph
 7
 8type Circuit[V: Hashable, E: Hashable] = Hypergraph[V, E, Terminals, Component]
 9
10def buildCircuit(components: Iterable[Component]) -> Circuit[str, str]:
11    """Turn a flat list of devices into the graph the solver works on.
12
13    Vertices are node names and edges are device names; each device reaches its nodes through its
14    own terminal roles (``component.terminals``), in the order of ``component.nodes``.
15    """
16    graph: Circuit[str, str] = Hypergraph()
17    for component in components:
18        if graph.hasEdge(component.name):
19            raise SpiceError(f"duplicate component name {component.name!r}", component.line)
20        if len(component.nodes) != len(component.terminals):
21            raise CircuitError(f"{component.name!r}: expected {len(component.terminals)} nodes, got {len(component.nodes)}")
22        graph.addEdge(component.name, component, dict(zip(component.terminals, component.nodes)))
23    return graph

circuit/circuitMath.py

 1import math
 2
 3_EXP_CLAMP = 40.0
 4
 5def exp(x: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
 6    """exp(x) and its derivative, continued linearly past _EXP_CLAMP to avoid overflow."""
 7    if x <= _EXP_CLAMP:
 8        e = math.exp(x)
 9        return e, e
10    e = math.exp(_EXP_CLAMP)
11    return e * (1.0 + x - _EXP_CLAMP), e
12
13def pnjlim(vnew: float, vold: float, vt: float, vcrit: float) -> float:
14    """SPICE's junction limiter: stop a forward-biased junction voltage leaping up the exponential."""
15    if vnew > vcrit and abs(vnew - vold) > 2.0 * vt:
16        if vold > 0.0:
17            arg = 1.0 + (vnew - vold) / vt
18            return vold + vt * math.log(arg) if arg > 0.0 else vcrit
19        return vt * math.log(vnew / vt)
20    return vnew
21
22def criticalVoltage(vt: float, isat: float) -> float:
23    return vt * math.log(vt / (math.sqrt(2.0) * isat))
24
25def squareLaw(vgs: float, vds: float, vth: float, k: float, lam: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
26    """NMOS drain current, gm and gds for vds >= 0."""
27    vov = vgs - vth
28    if vov <= 0.0:
29        return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
30    clm = 1.0 + lam * vds
31    if vds < vov:  # triode
32        base = vov * vds - 0.5 * vds * vds
33        return k * base * clm, k * vds * clm, k * (vov - vds) * clm + k * base * lam
34    half = 0.5 * k * vov * vov  # saturation
35    return half * clm, k * vov * clm, half * lam

 28_FET_STEP = 2.0  # largest change in a MOSFET control voltage per Newton iteration, volts
 29
 30def _add(matrix: FloatArray, i: int | None, j: int | None, value: float) -> None:
 31    """matrix[i, j] += value, where None means the ground row/column (which is dropped)."""
 32    if i is not None and j is not None:
 33        matrix[i, j] += value

 36# ---- parsing helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
 37
 38@dataclass(slots=True)
 39class ParseContext:
 40    """What a device needs to know about the rest of the netlist while it is being parsed."""
 41    models: Mapping[str, ModelCard]
 42    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list[str])
 43    _checked: set[str] = field(default_factory=set[str])
 44
 45    def warn(self, line: int, message: str) -> None:
 46        self.warnings.append(f"line {line}: {message}")
 47
 48    def model(self, device: str, line: int, modelName: str, kinds: tuple[str, ...]) -> ModelCard:
 49        card = self.models.get(modelName)
 50        if card is None:
 51            raise SpiceError(f"{device}: model {modelName!r} is not defined", line)
 52        if card.kind not in kinds:
 53            raise SpiceError(f"{device}: model {modelName!r} is a {card.kind} model, expected {' or '.join(kinds)}", line)
 54        return card
 55
 56    def checkModel(self, card: ModelCard, supported: frozenset[str], ignored: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> None:
 57        """Warn (once per card) about non-zero model parameters this simulator does not model."""
 58        if card.name in self._checked:
 59            return
 60        self._checked.add(card.name)
 61        for key, value in card.params.items():
 62            if key not in supported and key not in ignored and value != 0.0:
 63                self.warn(card.line, f".model {card.name}: parameter {key!r} is not modelled and was ignored")
 64
 65def _splitNodes(name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], count: int) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], list[str]]:
 66    if len(positional) < count:
 67        raise SpiceError(f"{name}: expected {count} nodes, got {len(positional)}", line)
 68    return tuple(canonicalNode(token) for token in positional[:count]), positional[count:]
 69
 70def _number(text: str, line: int, what: str) -> float:
 71    try:
 72        return parseValue(text)
 73    except ValueError:
 74        raise SpiceError(f"{what} {text!r} is not a number", line) from None
 75
 76def _only(name: str, line: int, parameters: dict[str, str], allowed: set[str]) -> None:
 77    for key in parameters:
 78        if key not in allowed:
 79            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: unsupported parameter {key!r}", line)
 80
 81def _single(name: str, line: int, rest: list[str], what: str) -> str:
 82    if len(rest) != 1:
 83        raise SpiceError(f"{name}: expected exactly one {what}, got {len(rest)} values", line)
 84    return rest[0]
 85
 86
 87# ---- independent source specification ---------------------------------------
 88
 89_SOURCE_FUNCTIONS = ("sin", "pulse", "pwl", "exp")
 90_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED = ("sffm", "am", "trnoise", "trrandom")
 91
 92def _waveform(name: str, line: int, kind: str, args: list[float]) -> Waveform:
 93    def need(low: int, high: int, usage: str) -> None:
 94        if not low <= len(args) <= high:
 95            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: {kind.upper()} needs {usage}", line)
 96
 97    try:
 98        match kind:
 99            case "sin":
100                need(3, 6, "vo va freq [td [theta [phase]]]")
101                vo, va, freq, td, theta, phase = (*args, *(0.0,) * (6 - len(args)))
102                if freq <= 0.0 or td < 0.0:
103                    raise SpiceError(f"{name}: SIN needs a positive frequency and a non-negative delay", line)
104                return sine(va, freq, offset=vo, phase=math.radians(phase), delay=td, damping=theta)
105            case "pulse":
106                need(2, 7, "v1 v2 [td [tr [tf [pw [per]]]]]")
107                v1, v2, td, tr, tf = (*args[:5], *(0.0,) * (5 - len(args[:5])))
108                pw = args[5] if len(args) > 5 else math.inf   # SPICE defaults this to TSTOP; "forever" is the closest equivalent
109                per = args[6] if len(args) > 6 and args[6] > 0.0 else None
110                if min(td, tr, tf, pw) < 0.0:
111                    raise SpiceError(f"{name}: PULSE times must not be negative", line)
112                return pulse(v1, v2, width=pw, delay=td, rise=tr, fall=tf, period=per)
113            case "pwl":
114                if len(args) < 2 or len(args) % 2:
115                    raise SpiceError(f"{name}: PWL needs time/value pairs", line)
116                return pwl(list(zip(args[0::2], args[1::2])))
117            case "exp":
118                need(6, 6, "v1 v2 td1 tau1 td2 tau2")
119                v1, v2, td1, tau1, td2, tau2 = args
120                return exponential(v1, v2, riseDelay=td1, riseTau=tau1, fallDelay=td2, fallTau=tau2)
121    except SpiceError:
122        raise
123    except ValueError as error:   # from the waveform constructors, e.g. PWL times out of order
124        raise SpiceError(f"{name}: {error}", line) from None
125    raise SpiceError(f"{name}: unsupported source function {kind!r}", line)
126
127def parseSource(name: str, line: int, tokens: list[str]) -> Source:
128    """Parse ``[dc] value [ac mag [phase]] [sin(...) | pulse(...) | pwl(...) | exp(...)]`` (lower-cased tokens)."""
129    dc: float | None = None
130    ac: complex = 0.0
131    waveform: Waveform | None = None
132
133    i = 0
134    while i < len(tokens):
135        token = tokens[i]
136        if token == "dc":
137            if dc is not None or i + 1 >= len(tokens):
138                raise SpiceError(f"{name}: DC needs exactly one value", line)
139            dc = _number(tokens[i + 1], line, "DC value")
140            i += 2
141        elif token == "ac":
142            if i + 1 >= len(tokens) or not isValue(tokens[i + 1]):
143                raise SpiceError(f"{name}: AC needs a magnitude", line)
144            magnitude = _number(tokens[i + 1], line, "AC magnitude")
145            i += 2
146            phase = 0.0
147            if i < len(tokens) and isValue(tokens[i]):
148                phase = _number(tokens[i], line, "AC phase")
149                i += 1
150            ac = cmath.rect(magnitude, math.radians(phase))
151        elif token in _SOURCE_FUNCTIONS:
152            if waveform is not None:
153                raise SpiceError(f"{name}: only one time-dependent function is allowed", line)
154            i += 1
155            args: list[float] = []
156            while i < len(tokens) and isValue(tokens[i]):
157                args.append(_number(tokens[i], line, f"{token.upper()} argument"))
158                i += 1
159            waveform = _waveform(name, line, token, args)
160        elif token in _SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED:
161            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: {token.upper()} sources are not supported", line)
162        elif i == 0 and isValue(token):
163            dc = _number(token, line, "DC value")
164            i += 1
165        else:
166            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: unexpected {token!r} in source specification", line)
167
168    if dc is None:
169        dc = waveform(0.0) if waveform is not None else 0.0   # as SPICE: a time-dependent source's DC value is its value at t = 0
170    return Source(dc, ac, waveform)
171

173# ---- devices ------------------------------------------------------------------
174
175@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
176class Branch[E: Hashable]:
177    """A linear device placed in the equations."""
178    edge: E
179    device: Component
180    row: int | None  # row/column of this device's branch current, if it has one
181    p: int | None    # index of the positive node, None if it is ground
182    n: int | None    # index of the negative node, None if it is ground
183
184@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
185class Component(ABC):
186    name: str
187    line: int
188    nodes: tuple[str, ...]  # one per entry of `terminals`, same order
189
190    letter: ClassVar[str]
191    terminals: ClassVar[type[Terminals]]
192    branchCurrent: ClassVar[bool] = False  # whether the device adds a branch-current unknown
193
194    @classmethod
195    @abstractmethod
196    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Component:
197        """Build the device from a netlist line already split into tokens.
198
199        `positional` holds the tokens without ``=`` (nodes first), `parameters` the ``key=value`` ones.
200        """
201        raise NotImplementedError
202
203    @abstractmethod
204    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
205        """Check the device's parameters, raising `CircuitError` if they cannot be simulated."""
206        raise NotImplementedError
207
208    def build[E: Hashable](self, edge: E, nodes: tuple[int | None, ...], row: int | None, gmin: float) -> Branch[E] | Nonlinear[E]:
209        """Place the device in the equations. `nodes` are unknown indices in terminal order (None = ground)
210        and `row` is the unknown reserved for its branch current (only given if `branchCurrent`)."""
211        return Branch(edge, self, row, nodes[0], nodes[1])
212
213    def stamp[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, C: FloatArray, contributions: list[tuple[int, float, Source]]) -> None:
214        """Write one linear device's equations into G, C and the right-hand-side description.
215
216        "Stamping" means each device adds a small fixed pattern to the matrices, so any circuit is
217        just the sum of its devices' stamps. Nodes on ground (None) are skipped by `_add`.
218        """
219        raise CircuitError(f"{branch.edge!r}: unsupported device {branch.device}")
220
221    def handleInitialConditions[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, b: FloatArray) -> None:
222        pass
223
224@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
225class Resistor(Component):
226    resistance: float   # ohms
227
228    letter = "R"
229    terminals = BranchTerminals
230
231    @classmethod
232    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Resistor:
233        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 2)
234        _only(name, line, parameters, set())
235        return cls(name, line, nodes, _number(_single(name, line, rest, "resistance"), line, "resistance"))
236
237    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
238        requirePositive(edge, "resistance", self.resistance)
239
240    def stamp[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, C: FloatArray, contributions: list[tuple[int, float, Source]]) -> None:
241        p, n = branch.p, branch.n
242        g: float = 1.0 / self.resistance
243        _add(G, p, p, g)
244        _add(G, n, n, g)
245        _add(G, p, n, -g)
246        _add(G, n, p, -g)
247
248@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
249class Capacitor(Component):
250    capacitance: float  # farads
251    initialVoltage: float = 0.0   # volts across p/n
252
253    letter = "C"
254    terminals = BranchTerminals
255    branchCurrent = True
256
257    @classmethod
258    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Capacitor:
259        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 2)
260        _only(name, line, parameters, {"ic"})
261        ic = _number(parameters["ic"], line, "initial voltage") if "ic" in parameters else 0.0
262        return cls(name, line, nodes, _number(_single(name, line, rest, "capacitance"), line, "capacitance"), ic)
263
264    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
265        requirePositive(edge, "capacitance", self.capacitance)
266        requireFinite(edge, "initial voltage", self.initialVoltage)
267
268    def stamp[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, C: FloatArray, contributions: list[tuple[int, float, Source]]) -> None:
269        p, n, row = branch.p, branch.n, branch.row
270        assert row is not None
271        _add(G, p, row, 1.0)
272        _add(G, n, row, -1.0)
273        G[row, row] += 1.0      # i - C d(v(p) - v(n))/dt = 0
274        _add(C, row, p, -self.capacitance)
275        _add(C, row, n, +self.capacitance)
276
277    def handleInitialConditions[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, b: FloatArray) -> None:
278        assert branch.row is not None
279        G[branch.row, :] = 0.0
280        _add(G, branch.row, branch.p, 1.0)
281        _add(G, branch.row, branch.n, -1.0)
282        b[branch.row] = self.initialVoltage
283
284@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
285class Inductor(Component):
286    inductance: float   # henries
287    initialCurrent: float = 0.0   # amps across p/n
288
289    letter = "L"
290    terminals = BranchTerminals
291    branchCurrent = True
292
293    @classmethod
294    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Inductor:
295        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 2)
296        _only(name, line, parameters, {"ic"})
297        ic = _number(parameters["ic"], line, "initial current") if "ic" in parameters else 0.0
298        return cls(name, line, nodes, _number(_single(name, line, rest, "inductance"), line, "inductance"), ic)
299
300    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
301        requirePositive(edge, "inductance", self.inductance)
302        requireFinite(edge, "initial current", self.initialCurrent)
303
304    def stamp[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, C: FloatArray, contributions: list[tuple[int, float, Source]]) -> None:
305        p, n, row = branch.p, branch.n, branch.row
306        assert row is not None
307        _add(G, p, row, 1.0)
308        _add(G, n, row, -1.0)
309        _add(G, row, p, 1.0)    # v(p) - v(n) - L di/dt = 0
310        _add(G, row, n, -1.0)
311        C[row, row] -= self.inductance
312
313    def handleInitialConditions[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, b: FloatArray) -> None:
314        assert branch.row is not None
315        G[branch.row, :] = 0.0
316        G[branch.row, branch.row] = 1.0
317        b[branch.row] = self.initialCurrent
318
319@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
320class VoltageSource(Component):
321    source: Source
322
323    letter = "V"
324    terminals = BranchTerminals
325    branchCurrent = True
326
327    @classmethod
328    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> VoltageSource:
329        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 2)
330        _only(name, line, parameters, set())
331        return cls(name, line, nodes, parseSource(name, line, rest))
332
333    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
334        requireFinite(edge, "dc value", self.source.dc)
335
336    def stamp[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, C: FloatArray, contributions: list[tuple[int, float, Source]]) -> None:
337        p, n, row = branch.p, branch.n, branch.row
338        assert row is not None
339        _add(G, p, row, 1.0)    # branch current leaves p ...
340        _add(G, n, row, -1.0)   # ... and enters n
341        _add(G, row, p, 1.0)    # v(p) - v(n) = V
342        _add(G, row, n, -1.0)
343        contributions.append((row, 1.0, self.source))
344
345@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
346class CurrentSource(Component):
347    source: Source
348
349    letter = "I"
350    terminals = BranchTerminals
351
352    @classmethod
353    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> CurrentSource:
354        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 2)
355        _only(name, line, parameters, set())
356        return cls(name, line, nodes, parseSource(name, line, rest))
357
358    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
359        requireFinite(edge, "dc value", self.source.dc)
360
361    def stamp[E: Hashable](self, branch: Branch[E], G: FloatArray, C: FloatArray, contributions: list[tuple[int, float, Source]]) -> None:
362        # the source pushes `value` from p through itself to n: it draws it out of node p and delivers it into node n
363        if branch.p is not None:
364            contributions.append((branch.p, -1.0, self.source))
365        if branch.n is not None:
366            contributions.append((branch.n, +1.0, self.source))
367
368@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
369class Diode(Component):
370    """Shockley diode: I = Is (exp(V / (n Vt)) - 1), anode -> cathode.
371
372    If `breakdownVoltage` is set the diode also conducts in reverse, reaching
373    `breakdownCurrent` when the reverse voltage equals `breakdownVoltage` (a Zener).
374    """
375    saturationCurrent: float = 1e-14  # Is, amps
376    emissionCoefficient: float = 1.0  # n
377    thermalVoltage: float = 0.02585   # Vt = kT/q, volts (about 300 K)
378    breakdownVoltage: float | None = None   # positive reverse voltage, volts
379    breakdownCurrent: float = 1e-3          # amps at the breakdown voltage
380
381    letter = "D"
382    terminals = DiodeTerminals
383
384    _MODEL: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"is", "n", "bv", "ibv"})
385    _IGNORED: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"level"})
386
387    @classmethod
388    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Diode:
389        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 2)
390        _only(name, line, parameters, set())
391        if len(rest) > 1:
392            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: unexpected {rest[1]!r} (the area factor is not supported)", line)
393        if not rest:
394            return cls(name, line, nodes)
395        card = context.model(name, line, rest[0], ("d",))
396        context.checkModel(card, cls._MODEL, cls._IGNORED)
397        p = card.params
398        return cls(
399            name, line, nodes,
400            saturationCurrent=p.get("is", 1e-14), emissionCoefficient=p.get("n", 1.0),
401            breakdownVoltage=p.get("bv"), breakdownCurrent=p.get("ibv", 1e-3),
402        )
403
404    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
405        requirePositive(edge, "saturation current", self.saturationCurrent)
406        requirePositive(edge, "emission coefficient", self.emissionCoefficient)
407        requirePositive(edge, "thermal voltage", self.thermalVoltage)
408        if self.breakdownVoltage is not None:
409            requirePositive(edge, "breakdown voltage", self.breakdownVoltage)
410        requirePositive(edge, "breakdown current", self.breakdownCurrent)
411
412    def build[E: Hashable](self, edge: E, nodes: tuple[int | None, ...], row: int | None, gmin: float) -> Nonlinear[E]:
413        vt = self.emissionCoefficient * self.thermalVoltage
414        isat, bv, ibv = self.saturationCurrent, self.breakdownVoltage, self.breakdownCurrent
415        vcrit = criticalVoltage(vt, isat)
416        vcritBd = criticalVoltage(vt, ibv)
417
418        def model(c: FloatArray) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
419            v = float(c[0])
420            e, de = exp(v / vt)
421            i = isat * (e - 1.0) + gmin * v
422            g = isat / vt * de + gmin
423            if bv is not None:
424                eb, deb = exp(-(v + bv) / vt)
425                i -= ibv * eb
426                g += ibv / vt * deb
427            return np.array([i, -i]), np.array([[g], [-g]])
428
429        def limit(new: FloatArray, old: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
430            v = pnjlim(float(new[0]), float(old[0]), vt, vcrit)
431            if bv is not None:  # same limiter, mirrored, for the reverse-breakdown exponential
432                arg = -(v + bv)
433                mirrored = pnjlim(arg, -(float(old[0]) + bv), vt, vcritBd)
434                if mirrored != arg:   # only touch v if limiting happened: rewriting it as -(-(v + bv)) - bv
435                    v = -mirrored - bv    # can differ by an ulp, which Newton would then read as "still limiting" forever
436            return np.array([v])
437
438        return Nonlinear(edge, self.terminals, nodes, 1.0, np.array([[1.0, -1.0]]), model, limit)
439
440@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
441class Bjt(Component):
442    """Transport (Ebers-Moll) bipolar transistor. Terminals: collector, base, emitter.
443
444    `earlyVoltage` (positive) adds output conductance; None means an ideal current source.
445    """
446    polarity: Literal["npn", "pnp"] = "npn"
447    saturationCurrent: float = 1e-14  # Is, amps
448    betaForward: float = 100.0
449    betaReverse: float = 1.0
450    earlyVoltage: float | None = None
451    thermalVoltage: float = 0.02585
452
453    letter = "Q"
454    terminals = BjtTerminals
455
456    _MODEL: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"is", "bf", "br", "vaf", "va"})
457    _IGNORED: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"level"})
458
459    @classmethod
460    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Bjt:
461        nodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 3)
462        _only(name, line, parameters, set())
463        if not rest:
464            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: a transistor needs a model name", line)
465        if len(rest) > 1:
466            raise SpiceError(f"{name}: unexpected {rest[1]!r} (substrate nodes and the area factor are not supported)", line)
467        card = context.model(name, line, rest[0], ("npn", "pnp"))
468        context.checkModel(card, cls._MODEL, cls._IGNORED)
469        p = card.params
470        return cls(
471            name, line, nodes, polarity="npn" if card.kind == "npn" else "pnp",
472            saturationCurrent=p.get("is", 1e-16), betaForward=p.get("bf", 100.0), betaReverse=p.get("br", 1.0),
473            earlyVoltage=p.get("vaf", p.get("va")) or None,   # 0 (SPICE's default) means "no Early effect"
474        )
475
476    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
477        requireValues(edge, "polarity", self.polarity, "npn", "pnp")
478        requirePositive(edge, "saturation current", self.saturationCurrent)
479        requirePositive(edge, "beta forward", self.betaForward)
480        requirePositive(edge, "beta reverse", self.betaReverse)
481        requirePositive(edge, "thermal voltage", self.thermalVoltage)
482        if self.earlyVoltage is not None:
483            requirePositive(edge, "early voltage", self.earlyVoltage)
484
485    def build[E: Hashable](self, edge: E, nodes: tuple[int | None, ...], row: int | None, gmin: float) -> Nonlinear[E]:
486        vt, isat, bf, br, va = self.thermalVoltage, self.saturationCurrent, self.betaForward, self.betaReverse, self.earlyVoltage
487        vcrit = criticalVoltage(vt, isat)
488
489        def model(c: FloatArray) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
490            vbe, vbc = float(c[0]), float(c[1])
491            ef, def_ = exp(vbe / vt)
492            er, der = exp(vbc / vt)
493            iF, iR = isat * (ef - 1.0), isat * (er - 1.0)
494            gF, gR = isat / vt * def_, isat / vt * der
495
496            qb, dqb = 1.0, 0.0  # Early-effect factor and its derivative with respect to vbc
497            if va is not None:
498                raw = 1.0 - vbc / va
499                qb, dqb = (raw, -1.0 / va) if raw > 1e-3 else (1e-3, 0.0)
500
501            ict = (iF - iR) * qb  # transport current, collector -> emitter
502            ic = ict - iR / br
503            ib = iF / bf + iR / br
504            dic = (gF * qb, -gR * qb + (iF - iR) * dqb - gR / br)
505            dib = (gF / bf, gR / br)
506
507            # gmin shunts across base-emitter (b -> e) and base-collector (b -> c)
508            ic -= gmin * vbc
509            ib += gmin * (vbe + vbc)
510            dic = (dic[0], dic[1] - gmin)
511            dib = (dib[0] + gmin, dib[1] + gmin)
512
513            currents = np.array([ic, ib, -(ic + ib)])
514            jacobian = np.array([
515                [dic[0], dic[1]],
516                [dib[0], dib[1]],
517                [-(dic[0] + dib[0]), -(dic[1] + dib[1])],
518            ])
519            return currents, jacobian
520
521        def limit(new: FloatArray, old: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
522            return np.array([
523                pnjlim(float(new[0]), float(old[0]), vt, vcrit),
524                pnjlim(float(new[1]), float(old[1]), vt, vcrit),
525            ])
526
527        # controls: vbe = Vb - Ve, vbc = Vb - Vc; terminals ordered (c, b, e)
528        T = np.array([[0.0, 1.0, -1.0], [-1.0, 1.0, 0.0]])
529        return Nonlinear(edge, self.terminals, nodes, 1.0 if self.polarity == "npn" else -1.0, T, model, limit)
530
531@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
532class Mosfet(Component):
533    """Level-1 (square law) MOSFET. Terminals: drain, gate, source (the bulk node of an ``M`` line is read and ignored).
534
535    threshold                    normalised threshold: conduction needs Vgs > threshold for
536                                 an NMOS and Vsg > threshold for a PMOS (so an enhancement
537                                 device has a positive value for both)
538    k                            Kp * W / L, in A/V^2: Id = k/2 (Vgs - Vth)^2 in saturation
539    channelLengthModulation      lambda, 1/V (0 for an ideal current source in saturation)
540    The device is symmetric: drain and source swap automatically if Vds reverses.
541    """
542    polarity: Literal["nmos", "pmos"] = "nmos"
543    threshold: float = 1.0
544    k: float = 2e-3
545    channelLengthModulation: float = 0.0
546
547    letter = "M"
548    terminals = MosfetTerminals
549
550    _MODEL: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"vto", "kp", "lambda", "level"})
551    _INSTANCE: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({"w", "l", "m", "ad", "as", "pd", "ps", "nrd", "nrs"})
552    _DEFAULT_SIZE: ClassVar[float] = 100e-6   # SPICE's default W and L, metres
553
554    @classmethod
555    def parse(cls, name: str, line: int, positional: list[str], parameters: dict[str, str], context: ParseContext) -> Mosfet:
556        allNodes, rest = _splitNodes(name, line, positional, 4)   # d g s b
557        _only(name, line, parameters, set(cls._INSTANCE))
558        modelName = _single(name, line, rest, "model name")
559        card = context.model(name, line, modelName, ("nmos", "pmos"))
560        context.checkModel(card, cls._MODEL)
561        if card.params.get("level", 1.0) != 1.0:
562            context.warn(card.line, f".model {card.name}: only level 1 is implemented, using level 1")
563
564        def size(key: str) -> float:
565            return _number(parameters[key], line, key) if key in parameters else cls._DEFAULT_SIZE
566        multiplier = _number(parameters["m"], line, "m") if "m" in parameters else 1.0
567
568        vto = card.params.get("vto", 0.0)
569        # SPICE writes a PMOS threshold as a negative number; this class normalises it to be positive
570        threshold = vto if card.kind == "nmos" else -vto
571        length = size("l")
572        k = card.params.get("kp", 2e-5) * multiplier * size("w") / length if length > 0.0 else 0.0
573        return cls(
574            name, line, allNodes[:3], polarity="nmos" if card.kind == "nmos" else "pmos",
575            threshold=threshold, k=k, channelLengthModulation=card.params.get("lambda", 0.0),
576        )
577
578    def validate(self, edge: object) -> None:
579        requireValues(edge, "polarity", self.polarity, "nmos", "pmos")
580        requireFinite(edge, "threshold", self.threshold)
581        requirePositive(edge, "k", self.k)
582        requireNonNegative(edge, "channel length modulation", self.channelLengthModulation)
583
584    def build[E: Hashable](self, edge: E, nodes: tuple[int | None, ...], row: int | None, gmin: float) -> Nonlinear[E]:
585        vth, k, lam = self.threshold, self.k, self.channelLengthModulation
586
587        def model(c: FloatArray) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
588            vgs, vds = float(c[0]), float(c[1])
589            if vds >= 0.0:
590                i, gm, gds = squareLaw(vgs, vds, vth, k, lam)
591            else:  # symmetric device: the channel runs the other way, source and drain swap
592                i2, gm2, gds2 = squareLaw(vgs - vds, -vds, vth, k, lam)
593                i, gm, gds = -i2, -gm2, gm2 + gds2
594            i += gmin * vds
595            gds += gmin
596            currents = np.array([i, 0.0, -i])
597            jacobian = np.array([[gm, gds], [0.0, 0.0], [-gm, -gds]])
598            return currents, jacobian
599
600        def limit(new: FloatArray, old: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
601            delta = new - old
602            return np.where(np.abs(delta) <= _FET_STEP, new, old + np.sign(delta) * _FET_STEP)
603
604        # controls: vgs = Vg - Vs, vds = Vd - Vs; terminals ordered (d, g, s)
605        T = np.array([[0.0, 1.0, -1.0], [1.0, 0.0, -1.0]])
606        return Nonlinear(edge, self.terminals, nodes, 1.0 if self.polarity == "nmos" else -1.0, T, model, limit)
607
608
609# Which class reads which netlist letter. An explicit table rather than `Component.__subclasses__()`, because
610# `@dataclass(slots=True)` creates a second class object and the stale one can show up in `__subclasses__()`.
611COMPONENT_TYPES: dict[str, type[Component]] = {
612    cls.letter.lower(): cls
613    for cls in (Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, VoltageSource, CurrentSource, Diode, Bjt, Mosfet)
614}

gui/gui.py

  1"""Graphical front end: pick a netlist in the system file dialog, run it, browse tables and plots.
  2
  3The simulation itself runs on a worker thread (`runNetlist`) so the window never freezes; its result comes
  4back through a queue that the Tk thread polls. `runNetlist` touches no widgets, so it is testable on its own.
  5"""
  6from __future__ import annotations
  7
  8import queue
  9import threading
 10from dataclasses import dataclass
 11from pathlib import Path
 12from tkinter import filedialog
 13from tkinter import font as tkfont
 14from typing import Any, Literal
 15
 16import customtkinter as ctk
 17from matplotlib.backends.backend_tkagg import FigureCanvasTkAgg, NavigationToolbar2Tk
 18
 19from errors import CircuitError, ProbeError, SimulationError, SpiceError
 20from gui.plotting import makeFigure
 21from probes import probesFor
 22from report import formatTable, writeCsv
 23from simulate import Solution, simulate
 24from spiceParser import parseNetlist
 25
 26type Method = Literal["trapezoidal", "backward_euler"]
 27
 28ctk.set_appearance_mode("system")   # follow the operating system's light/dark setting
 29ctk.set_default_color_theme("blue")
 30
 31_FILETYPES = [("SPICE netlists", "*.cir *.sp *.spice *.net *.ckt *.txt"), ("All files", "*.*")]
 32_TEXT_ROWS = 2000   # the Results tab shows at most this many rows; CSV export has them all
 33_MONO_CANDIDATES = ("Cascadia Mono", "Consolas", "Menlo", "DejaVu Sans Mono", "Liberation Mono", "Courier New")
 34
 35
 36# ---- work that needs no widgets -----------------------------------------------
 37
 38@dataclass(frozen=True)
 39class AnalysisView:
 40    """One analysis ready to display: its solution, the probes to show, and the rendered table."""
 41    label: str
 42    solution: Solution
 43    probes: tuple[str, ...]
 44    text: str
 45
 46@dataclass(frozen=True)
 47class Loaded:
 48    title: str
 49    source: str
 50    views: list[AnalysisView]
 51    warnings: list[str]
 52
 53def runNetlist(path: Path, method: Method) -> Loaded:
 54    """Parse and simulate `path`, rendering every table. Raises the simulator's own errors unchanged."""
 55    netlist = parseNetlist(str(path))
 56    solutions, warnings = simulate(netlist, method=method)
 57    views = []
 58    for number, solution in enumerate(solutions, start=1):
 59        probes = probesFor(solution, netlist.prints)
 60        views.append(AnalysisView(f"{number}: .{solution.analysis.kind}", solution, probes,
 61                                  formatTable(solution, probes, maxRows=_TEXT_ROWS)))
 62    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
 63    return Loaded(netlist.title, source, views, warnings)
 64
 65def numberedSource(source: str) -> str:
 66    """The netlist with line numbers, so 'line 7' in an error message can be found at a glance."""
 67    return "\n".join(f"{number:>4}  {line}" for number, line in enumerate(source.splitlines(), start=1))
 68
 69def _monoFamily(root: Any) -> str:
 70    try:
 71        available = set(tkfont.families(root))
 72        for family in _MONO_CANDIDATES:
 73            if family in available:
 74                return family
 75        return str(tkfont.nametofont("TkFixedFont").actual("family"))
 76    except Exception:   # a missing font must never stop the window opening
 77        return "Courier"
 78
 79
 80# ---- the window -------------------------------------------------------------------
 81
 82class App(ctk.CTk):
 83    def __init__(self, initialPath: str | None = None) -> None:
 84        super().__init__()
 85        self.title("SPICE Solver")
 86        self.geometry("1180x740")
 87        self.minsize(940, 580)
 88
 89        self.path: Path | None = None
 90        self.method: Method = "trapezoidal"
 91        self.views: list[AnalysisView] = []
 92        self.current = 0
 93        self._busy = False
 94        self._outcomes: queue.Queue[tuple[str, Any]] = queue.Queue()
 95        self._canvas: FigureCanvasTkAgg | None = None
 96        self._toolbar: NavigationToolbar2Tk | None = None
 97        self._mono = ctk.CTkFont(family=_monoFamily(self), size=13)
 98
 99        self._build()
100        self.bind("<Control-o>", lambda _event: self.openFile())
101        self.bind("<F5>", lambda _event: self.run())
102        if initialPath:
103            self.after(100, lambda: self.load(Path(initialPath)))
104
105    # ---- layout
106
107    def _build(self) -> None:
108        self.grid_columnconfigure(1, weight=1)
109        self.grid_rowconfigure(0, weight=1)
110
111        side = ctk.CTkFrame(self, width=250, corner_radius=0)

175    def _textbox(self, tab: str) -> ctk.CTkTextbox:
176        box = ctk.CTkTextbox(self.tabs.tab(tab), font=self._mono, wrap="none", state="disabled")
177        box.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky="nsew")

179
180    # ---- helpers
181
182    @staticmethod
183    def _setText(box: ctk.CTkTextbox, text: str) -> None:
184        box.configure(state="normal")
185        box.delete("1.0", "end")
186        box.insert("1.0", text)
187        box.configure(state="disabled")
188
189    def _setStatus(self, text: str, error: bool = False) -> None:
190        self.status.configure(text=text, text_color=("#c0392b", "#ff6b5e") if error else ("gray40", "gray65"))
191
192    def _setBusy(self, busy: bool) -> None:
193        self._busy = busy
194        if busy:
195            self.progress.grid()
196            self.progress.start()
197        else:
198            self.progress.stop()
199            self.progress.grid_remove()
200        state = "disabled" if busy else "normal"
201        self.openButton.configure(state=state)
202        self.runButton.configure(state="disabled" if busy or self.path is None else "normal")
203
204    def _setMethod(self, method: str) -> None:
205        self.method = "backward_euler" if method == "backward_euler" else "trapezoidal"
206
207    def _setAppearance(self, mode: str) -> None:
208        ctk.set_appearance_mode(mode.lower())
209        self._renderPlot()   # the figure draws its own colours, so it has to be rebuilt
210
211    # ---- opening and running
212
213    def openFile(self) -> None:
214        """Show the system's file explorer and load whatever the user picks."""
215        chosen = filedialog.askopenfilename(
216            title="Open SPICE netlist", filetypes=_FILETYPES,
217            initialdir=str(self.path.parent) if self.path else None,
218        )
219        if chosen:
220            self.load(Path(chosen))
221
222    def load(self, path: Path) -> None:
223        self.path = path
224        self.fileLabel.configure(text=path.name)
225        self.run()
226
227    def run(self) -> None:
228        if self.path is None or self._busy:
229            return
230        self._setBusy(True)
231        self._setStatus(f"Simulating {self.path.name}…")
232        threading.Thread(target=self._work, args=(self.path, self.method), daemon=True).start()
233        self.after(80, self._poll)
234
235    def _work(self, path: Path, method: Method) -> None:
236        """Worker thread: no widgets here, only the queue."""
237        try:
238            self._outcomes.put(("ok", runNetlist(path, method)))
239        except (SpiceError, SimulationError, CircuitError, ProbeError) as error:
240            self._outcomes.put(("error", str(error)))
241        except OSError as error:
242            self._outcomes.put(("error", f"cannot read {path}: {error.strerror or error}"))
243        except Exception as error:   # keep the window usable whatever goes wrong inside the simulator
244            self._outcomes.put(("error", f"unexpected {type(error).__name__}: {error}"))
245
246    def _poll(self) -> None:
247        try:
248            kind, payload = self._outcomes.get_nowait()
249        except queue.Empty:
250            self.after(80, self._poll)
251            return
252        self._setBusy(False)
253        if kind == "error":
254            self._showError(payload)
255        else:
256            self._showLoaded(payload)
257
258    # ---- showing results
259
260    def _showError(self, message: str) -> None:
261        self._setText(self.messages, f"Error\n\n{message}\n")
262        self.tabs.set("Messages")
263        self._setStatus(message.splitlines()[0], error=True)
264
265    def _showLoaded(self, loaded: Loaded) -> None:
266        self.views = loaded.views
267        self.current = 0
268        self.heading.configure(text=loaded.title or (self.path.name if self.path else ""))
269        self._setText(self.netlistBox, numberedSource(loaded.source))
270        self._setText(self.messages, "\n".join(f"warning: {w}" for w in loaded.warnings) or "No warnings.")
271
272        if len(self.views) > 1:
273            self.selector.configure(values=[v.label for v in self.views])
274            self.selector.set(self.views[0].label)
275            self.selector.grid()
276        else:
277            self.selector.grid_remove()
278
279        self.exportButton.configure(state="normal")
280        self._showCurrent()
281        self.tabs.set("Results")
282        count = len(loaded.warnings)
283        self._setStatus(f"Done: {len(self.views)} analysis(es)" + (f", {count} warning(s) in the Messages tab." if count else "."))
284
285    def _select(self, label: str) -> None:
286        self.current = next((k for k, v in enumerate(self.views) if v.label == label), 0)
287        self._showCurrent()
288
289    def _showCurrent(self) -> None:
290        self._setText(self.results, self.views[self.current].text)
291        self._renderPlot()
292
293    def _renderPlot(self) -> None:
294        if not self.views:
295            return
296        if self._canvas is not None:
297            self._canvas.get_tk_widget().destroy()
298            self._canvas = None
299        if self._toolbar is not None:
300            self._toolbar.destroy()
301            self._toolbar = None
302        self.plotNote.pack_forget()
303
304        view = self.views[self.current]
305        try:
306            figure = makeFigure(view.solution, view.probes, dark=ctk.get_appearance_mode() == "Dark")
307        except Exception as error:   # a plotting problem should not hide the numeric results
308            self.plotNote.configure(text=f"Could not draw this plot: {error}")
309            self.plotNote.pack(expand=True)
310            return
311        self._canvas = FigureCanvasTkAgg(figure, master=self.plotHolder)
312        self._toolbar = NavigationToolbar2Tk(self._canvas, self.plotHolder, pack_toolbar=False)
313        self._toolbar.update()
314        self._toolbar.pack(side="bottom", fill="x")
315        self._canvas.get_tk_widget().pack(side="top", fill="both", expand=True)
316        self._canvas.draw()
317
318    def exportCsv(self) -> None:
319        if not self.views or self.path is None:
320            return
321        view = self.views[self.current]
322        chosen = filedialog.asksaveasfilename(
323            title="Export CSV", defaultextension=".csv", filetypes=[("CSV files", "*.csv"), ("All files", "*.*")],
324            initialfile=f"{self.path.stem}_{view.solution.analysis.kind}.csv", initialdir=str(self.path.parent),
325        )
326        if not chosen:
327            return
328        try:
329            writeCsv(Path(chosen), view.solution, view.probes)
330        except OSError as error:
331            self._setStatus(f"Could not save {chosen}: {error.strerror or error}", error=True)
332        else:
333            self._setStatus(f"Saved {chosen}")

gui/plotting.py

 1"""Build matplotlib figures for a `Solution`. Needs no GUI toolkit, so it can be tested and reused anywhere.
 2
 3Probes are grouped by function (all ``v(..)`` together, ``vdb(..)`` and ``vp(..)`` each on their own axes,
 4and so on) so that quantities with different units never share a y axis.
 5"""
 6from matplotlib.axes import Axes
 7from matplotlib.figure import Figure
 8
 9from circuit.components import VoltageSource
10from probes import evaluate
11from simulate import Solution
12from spiceParser import AcAnalysis, OpAnalysis
13
14_PALETTE = ("#4c9be8", "#f08a4b", "#58b368", "#d9534f", "#a77bd8", "#c9a227", "#3fb5b5", "#e377c2")
15_MAX_PLOT_POINTS = 20_000   # longer traces are thinned for display (a CSV export keeps every point)
16
17def groupProbes(probes: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
18    """Probes by function name, in order of first appearance: ``{"v": ["v(a)", "v(b)"], "i": ["i(v1)"]}``."""
19    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
20    for probe in probes:
21        groups.setdefault(probe.split("(", 1)[0], []).append(probe)
22    return groups
23
24def yLabel(function: str) -> str:
25    if function.endswith("db"):
26        return "Magnitude (dB)"
27    if function in ("vp", "ip"):
28        return "Phase (°)"
29    return "Voltage (V)" if function.startswith("v") else "Current (A)"
30
31def xLabel(solution: Solution) -> str:
32    match solution.axisName:
33        case "time":
34            return "Time (s)"
35        case "frequency":
36            return "Frequency (Hz)"
37        case name:
38            device = solution.devices.get(name)
39            return f"{name} ({'V' if isinstance(device, VoltageSource) else 'A'})"
40
41def _style(ax: Axes, dark: bool) -> None:
42    text, grid, background = ("#e6e6e6", "#5a5a5a", "#2b2b2b") if dark else ("#1a1a1a", "#b0b0b0", "#f4f4f4")
43    ax.set_facecolor(background)
44    ax.tick_params(colors=text)
45    ax.xaxis.label.set_color(text)
46    ax.yaxis.label.set_color(text)
47    ax.title.set_color(text)
48    for side, spine in ax.spines.items():
49        spine.set_color(grid)
50        spine.set_visible(side in ("left", "bottom"))
51    ax.grid(True, color=grid, alpha=0.4, linewidth=0.7)
52
53def makeFigure(solution: Solution, probes: tuple[str, ...], dark: bool = False) -> Figure:
54    """One axes per probe function: lines against the sweep axis, or bars for an operating point."""
55    figure = Figure(figsize=(8.0, 5.6), dpi=100, facecolor="#2b2b2b" if dark else "#ebebeb", layout="constrained")
56    groups = groupProbes(probes)
57    isOp = isinstance(solution.analysis, OpAnalysis)
58    axes = figure.subplots(len(groups), 1, sharex=not isOp, squeeze=False)[:, 0]
59    text = "#e6e6e6" if dark else "#1a1a1a"
60
61    stride = max(1, solution.axis.size // _MAX_PLOT_POINTS)
62    for ax, (function, names) in zip(axes, groups.items()):
63        _style(ax, dark)
64        if isOp:
65            values = [float(evaluate(name, solution)[0]) for name in names]
66            ax.bar(names, values, color=[_PALETTE[k % len(_PALETTE)] for k in range(len(names))], width=0.6)
67            ax.axhline(0.0, color=text, linewidth=0.8)
68            ax.set_xlim(-0.6, max(len(names), 3) - 0.4)   # a lone bar should not fill the whole axes
69            if len(names) > 6:
70                ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=45)
71        else:
72            for k, name in enumerate(names):
73                ax.plot(solution.axis[::stride], evaluate(name, solution)[::stride], label=name,
74                        color=_PALETTE[k % len(_PALETTE)], linewidth=1.7)
75            legend = ax.legend(loc="best", frameon=False)
76            for entry in legend.get_texts():
77                entry.set_color(text)
78            if isinstance(solution.analysis, AcAnalysis) and solution.analysis.variation != "lin":
79                ax.set_xscale("log")
80        ax.set_ylabel(yLabel(function))
81
82    if not isOp:
83        axes[-1].set_xlabel(xLabel(solution))
84    return figure

solver/nonlinearDeviceModels.py

 1from collections.abc import Callable, Hashable
 2from dataclasses import dataclass
 3
 4from circuit.terminals import Terminals
 5from solver.waveformHelpers import FloatArray
 6
 7# ---- nonlinear device models -------------------------------------------------
 8#
 9# Every nonlinear device is described in a normalised frame so that one piece of
10# Newton/stamping code serves all of them:
11#
12#   terminals  the nodes it touches, in role order
13#   controls   the voltages the model depends on, c = sign * (T @ terminal voltages)
14#   model      c -> (terminal currents into the device, Jacobian d(currents)/d(c))
15#   limit      (new c, previous c) -> a c whose step is safe for Newton
16#
17# `sign` is +1 for NPN/NMOS/diode and -1 for PNP/PMOS, which are mirror images.
18
19type DeviceModel = Callable[[FloatArray], tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]]
20type Limiter = Callable[[FloatArray, FloatArray], FloatArray]
21
22@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
23class Nonlinear[E: Hashable]:
24    edge: E
25    roles: type[Terminals]
26    nodes: tuple[int | None, ...]  # unknown index per role, None for ground
27    sign: float
28    T: FloatArray                  # (controls x terminals) raw voltage differences
29    model: DeviceModel
30    limit: Limiter

 7    reltol: float = 1e-6         # relative tolerance on every unknown
 8    vntol: float = 1e-9          # absolute tolerance on node voltages, volts

 1from collections.abc import Hashable, Mapping
 2from dataclasses import dataclass
 3
 4from circuit.terminals import Terminals
 5from solver.waveformHelpers import ComplexArray, FloatArray
 6
 7@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
 8class DcResult[V: Hashable, E: Hashable]:
 9    voltages: Mapping[V, float]  # every vertex, ground = 0
10    currents: Mapping[E, float]  # every two-terminal device, first role -> second role
11    terminalCurrents: Mapping[E, Mapping[Terminals, float]]  # every device: current into each role
12
13@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
14class AcResult[V: Hashable, E: Hashable]:
15    frequencies: FloatArray  # hertz
16    voltages: Mapping[V, ComplexArray]  # complex phasors, one value per frequency
17    currents: Mapping[E, ComplexArray]
18    terminalCurrents: Mapping[E, Mapping[Terminals, ComplexArray]]
19
20@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
21class TransientResult[V: Hashable, E: Hashable]:
22    times: FloatArray  # seconds
23    voltages: Mapping[V, FloatArray]  # one value per time point
24    currents: Mapping[E, FloatArray]
25    terminalCurrents: Mapping[E, Mapping[Terminals, FloatArray]]

solver/solver.py

  1"""Circuit solver (modified nodal analysis + Newton iteration) on top of `Hypergraph`.
  2
  3Devices
  4-------
  5    Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, VoltageSource, CurrentSource     linear
  6    Diode (with optional Zener breakdown), Bjt (NPN/PNP), Mosfet (NMOS/PMOS)
  7
  8Analyses
  9--------
 10    solveDc         operating point (capacitors open, inductors shorted)
 11    solveAc         small-signal frequency response around the DC operating point
 12    solveTransient  time-domain response (fixed step, trapezoidal or backward Euler)
 13
 14Describing a circuit
 15--------------------
 16Use a `Circuit` (a `Hypergraph` whose roles are terminal enums and whose payloads are
 17`Component`s). Vertices are nets (any hashable), edges are devices (any hashable key) and
 18every device must be attached through exactly the terminals in its class's `terminals` enum:
 19
 20    Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor,
 21    VoltageSource, CurrentSource     BranchTerminals.POSITIVE, NEGATIVE
 22    Diode                            DiodeTerminals.ANODE, CATHODE
 23    Bjt                              BjtTerminals.COLLECTOR, BASE, EMITTER
 24    Mosfet                           MosfetTerminals.DRAIN, GATE, SOURCE
 25
 26`buildCircuit(components)` does this wiring from each component's `nodes`. By hand:
 27
 28    g = buildCircuit([
 29        VoltageSource("v1", 0, ("in", "0"), Source(dc=5.0, ac=1.0)),
 30        Resistor("r1", 0, ("in", "out"), 1e3),
 31        Diode("d1", 0, ("out", "0")),
 32    ])
 33
 34    op = solveDc(g, ground="0")
 35    ac = solveAc(g, ground="0", frequencies=logSweep(1, 1e6, 20))
 36    tr = solveTransient(g, ground="0", stop=5e-3, step=1e-6)
 37
 38Results
 39-------
 40Each result holds `voltages` (per vertex, ground = 0), `currents` (per two-terminal
 41device, flowing from its first role through the device to its second) and
 42`terminalCurrents` (per device, per role: the current flowing *into* the device
 43through that terminal, which is the only way to describe a transistor).
 44A voltage source that is delivering power therefore reports a negative current.
 45A current source pushes `value` from "p" through itself to "n".
 46
 47How it works
 48------------
 49Unknowns are every non-ground node voltage plus one branch current for each
 50voltage source, inductor and capacitor. Linear devices stamp into two matrices,
 51
 52        G x + C dx/dt + i_nl(x) = b(t)
 53
 54where i_nl are the nonlinear device currents. With no nonlinear devices this is
 55solved directly (DC: one solve; AC: one solve per frequency; transient: one LU
 56factorisation reused every step).
 57
 58With nonlinear devices each solve becomes a Newton iteration. Every iteration
 59replaces each device by its tangent: a conductance matrix (the Jacobian) plus an
 60equivalent current source, i.e. a linear circuit, which is stamped and solved like
 61any other. To stop the exponentials overflowing, junction voltages are limited to
 62a bounded change per iteration (SPICE's `pnjlim`; MOSFET voltages are step-clamped).
 63If plain Newton fails for the DC point, the solver retries with gmin stepping and
 64then source stepping; a failed transient step is retried as two half steps.
 65
 66Model limitations
 67-----------------
 68Device models are purely resistive (static). Add `Capacitor` edges for junction or
 69gate capacitance, and `Resistor` edges for series resistance. The MOSFET is level 1
 70(square law, channel-length modulation, no body effect, so no "b" terminal) and
 71the BJT is a transport (Ebers-Moll) model with an optional Early effect. All are
 72evaluated at a fixed temperature through `thermalVoltage`.
 73
 74Requires Python 3.12+, numpy and scipy.
 75"""
 76from __future__ import annotations
 77
 78import math
 79import warnings
 80from collections.abc import Hashable, Sequence
 81from typing import Any, Literal
 82
 83import numpy as np
 84from numpy.typing import NDArray
 85from scipy.linalg import LinAlgWarning, lu_factor, lu_solve
 86
 87from circuit.circuit import Circuit
 88from errors import CircuitError, ConvergenceError
 89from solver.nonlinearDeviceModels import Nonlinear
 90from solver.options import NewtonOptions
 91from solver.results import AcResult, DcResult, TransientResult
 92from solver.system import SINGULAR as _SINGULAR, System, solve
 93from solver.waveformHelpers import FloatArray
 94
 95
 96# ---- analyses --------------------------------------------------------------
 97
 98def solveDc[V: Hashable, E: Hashable](
 99    circuit: Circuit[V, E], ground: V, *, gmin: float = 1e-12,
100    options: NewtonOptions = NewtonOptions(),
101) -> DcResult[V, E]:
102    """DC operating point using each source's `dc` value.
103
104    `gmin` is a tiny conductance from every node to ground (and across every
105    device junction) that keeps otherwise floating nodes solvable. It perturbs
106    results by roughly gmin * (resistance), about 1e-9 relative for kilohm circuits.
107    """
108    system = System(circuit, ground, gmin)
109    x = system.operatingPoint(system.G, system.rhs(lambda s: s.dc), options)
110    voltages, currents, terminals = system.unpack(
111        x[None, :], lambda s: np.array([s.dc]), system.exactCurrents,
112    )
113    return DcResult(
114        {vertex: float(values[0]) for vertex, values in voltages.items()},
115        {edge: float(values[0]) for edge, values in currents.items()},
116        {edge: {role: float(values[0]) for role, values in roles.items()} for edge, roles in terminals.items()},
117    )
118
119
120def solveAc[V: Hashable, E: Hashable](
121    circuit: Circuit[V, E], ground: V, frequencies: Sequence[float] | FloatArray,
122    *, gmin: float = 1e-12, options: NewtonOptions = NewtonOptions(),
123) -> AcResult[V, E]:
124    """Small-signal response at each frequency (hertz), driven by each source's `ac` phasor.
125
126    Nonlinear devices are linearised around the DC operating point (found from each
127    source's `dc` value), so a transistor contributes its gm and output conductance.
128    """
129    f: FloatArray = np.asarray(frequencies, dtype=np.float64)
130    if f.ndim != 1 or f.size == 0 or not np.all(np.isfinite(f)) or np.any(f < 0.0):
131        raise CircuitError("frequencies must be a non-empty 1-D sequence of finite values >= 0")
132
133    system = System(circuit, ground, gmin)
134    g = system.G
135    jacobians: dict[E, FloatArray] = {}
136    if system.nonlinear:
137        operating = system.operatingPoint(system.G, system.rhs(lambda s: s.dc), options)
138        lin = system.linearize(operating, None)
139        g = g + lin.jacobian
140        jacobians = {dev.edge: lin.perDevice[k] for k, dev in enumerate(system.nonlinear)}
141
142    omega = 2.0 * np.pi * f
143    A = g[None, :, :] + 1j * omega[:, None, None] * system.C[None, :, :]
144    b = np.broadcast_to(system.rhsAc(), (f.size, system.size))
145    X = solve(A, b[..., None])[..., 0]
146
147    def smallSignalCurrents(dev: Nonlinear[E], X: NDArray[Any]) -> NDArray[Any]:
148        v = np.array([np.zeros(X.shape[0]) if node is None else X[:, node] for node in dev.nodes])
149        out: NDArray[Any] = jacobians[dev.edge] @ v
150        return out
151
152    voltages, currents, terminals = system.unpack(
153        X, lambda s: np.full(f.size, s.ac, dtype=np.complex128), smallSignalCurrents,
154    )
155    return AcResult(f, voltages, currents, terminals)
156
157
158def _transientLinear(system: System[Any, Any], x0: FloatArray, times: FloatArray,
159                     step: float, trapezoidal: bool) -> FloatArray:
160    """Fixed-step integration of G x + C dx/dt = b, factorising the step matrix once."""
161    G, C = system.G, system.C
162    scale = (2.0 if trapezoidal else 1.0) / step
163    with warnings.catch_warnings():
164        warnings.simplefilter("error", LinAlgWarning)
165        try:
166            lu = lu_factor(G + scale * C)
167        except (LinAlgWarning, ValueError) as error:
168            raise CircuitError(_SINGULAR) from error
169    history = scale * C - (G if trapezoidal else 0.0)
170
171    X: FloatArray = np.empty((times.size, system.size))
172    X[0] = x0
173    bPrevious = system.rhsAt(0.0)
174    for k in range(1, times.size):
175        b = system.rhsAt(float(times[k]))
176        rhs = b + bPrevious + history @ X[k - 1] if trapezoidal else b + history @ X[k - 1]
177        X[k] = lu_solve(lu, rhs)
178        bPrevious = b
179    return X
180
181
182def _transientNonlinear(system: System[Any, Any], x0: FloatArray, times: FloatArray, step: float,
183                        trapezoidal: bool, options: NewtonOptions) -> FloatArray:
184    """Fixed-step integration with a Newton solve per step; a failing step is retried as two half steps."""
185    G, C = system.G, system.C
186
187    def advance(
188        xPrev: FloatArray, bPrev: FloatArray, iPrev: FloatArray, t0: float, h: float, depth: int,
189    ) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray, FloatArray]:
190        b = system.rhsAt(t0 + h)
191        if trapezoidal:
192            a = G + (2.0 / h) * C
193            r = b + bPrev + ((2.0 / h) * C - G) @ xPrev - iPrev
194        else:
195            a = G + C / h
196            r = b + (C / h) @ xPrev
197        try:
198            x1 = system.newton(a, r, xPrev, options)
199        except ConvergenceError as error:
200            if depth >= options.maxStepHalvings:
201                raise ConvergenceError(
202                    f"transient analysis failed to converge near t = {t0 + h:g} s ({error})"
203                ) from error
204            xMid, bMid, iMid = advance(xPrev, bPrev, iPrev, t0, h / 2.0, depth + 1)
205            return advance(xMid, bMid, iMid, t0 + h / 2.0, h / 2.0, depth + 1)
206        return x1, b, system.nonlinearCurrents(x1)
207
208    X: FloatArray = np.empty((times.size, system.size))
209    x, b, i = x0, system.rhsAt(0.0), system.nonlinearCurrents(x0)
210    X[0] = x
211    for k in range(1, times.size):
212        x, b, i = advance(x, b, i, float(times[k - 1]), float(times[k] - times[k - 1]), 0)
213        X[k] = x
214    return X
215
216
217def solveTransient[V: Hashable, E: Hashable](
218    circuit: Circuit[V, E], ground: V, *, stop: float, step: float,
219    method: Literal["trapezoidal", "backward_euler"] = "trapezoidal",
220    useInitialConditions: bool = False, gmin: float = 1e-12,
221    options: NewtonOptions = NewtonOptions(),
222) -> TransientResult[V, E]:
223    """Time-domain response from t = 0 with a fixed time `step`.
224
225    Sources follow their `waveform` (or `dc` if they have none). `stop` is
226    rounded up to a whole number of steps.
227
228    Initial state:
229        useInitialConditions=False  start from the DC operating point at t = 0
230        useInitialConditions=True   start from each capacitor's `initialVoltage`
231                                    and each inductor's `initialCurrent`
232
233    Trapezoidal is second-order accurate but rings if the source jumps at t = 0
234    or between steps; backward_euler is first-order but heavily damped, so it is
235    the safer choice for stiff circuits or discontinuous drive.
236
237    With nonlinear devices every step runs a Newton iteration (see NewtonOptions),
238    and a step that fails to converge is automatically retried as two half steps.
239    """
240    if not (math.isfinite(stop) and math.isfinite(step) and 0.0 < step <= stop):
241        raise CircuitError("need finite values with 0 < step <= stop")
242    if method not in ("trapezoidal", "backward_euler"):
243        raise CircuitError(f"unknown method {method!r}")
244    trapezoidal = method == "trapezoidal"
245
246    system = System(circuit, ground, gmin)
247    steps = max(1, math.ceil(stop / step - 1e-9))
248    times: FloatArray = np.arange(steps + 1, dtype=np.float64) * step
249
250    if useInitialConditions:
251        Gic, bic = system.initialConditionSystem()
252        x0 = system.operatingPoint(Gic, bic, options)
253    else:
254        x0 = system.operatingPoint(system.G, system.rhsAt(0.0), options)
255
256    if system.nonlinear:
257        x = _transientNonlinear(system, x0, times, step, trapezoidal, options)
258    else:
259        x = _transientLinear(system, x0, times, step, trapezoidal)
260
261    if not np.all(np.isfinite(x)):
262        raise CircuitError(_SINGULAR)
263
264    return TransientResult(times, *system.unpack(
265        x, lambda s: np.array([s.at(float(t)) for t in times]), system.exactCurrents,
266    ))
